title: Period and Graph of y = sin(x/2)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the fundamental period of the function y = \sin(x/2) and describe the key points of its graph over one complete cycle.

steps.title: Calculate the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: In y = sin((1/2)x), the angular frequency is omega = 1/2, which stretches the standard period 2*pi by a factor of 2 to B = 4*pi.
steps.why: The function completes one full oscillation as x/2 ranges from 0 to 2*pi, i.e., as x ranges from 0 to 4*pi.

steps.title: Determine Amplitude and Range
steps.explanation: The amplitude is 1, so the graph oscillates vertically between -1 and 1.
steps.why: Horizontal scaling alters the period without changing the vertical range [-1, 1].

steps.title: Identify Quarter-Period Landmarks on [0, 4*pi]
steps.explanation: The quarter-period step is 4*pi/4 = pi, yielding zeros at 0, 2*pi, 4*pi, a peak of 1 at x = pi, and a trough of -1 at x = 3*pi.
steps.why: Evaluating sin(x/2) at multiples of pi maps directly to the quadrantal angles 0, pi/2, pi, 3*pi/2, and 2*pi.
